note: Human-verified ICB events that live only in board-paper PDFs or committee minutes, which scripts/refresh_icb_watch.py does not parse. Every entry must carry https sources and the date a person read them (verifiedOn); verify.py refuses one without. Quote or paraphrase only what the named document says. Add, never back-date.

events.headline: Birmingham and Solihull and Black Country Integrated Care Boards: redundancy business cases approved, notices issued from 1 September
events.detail: The chief executive's report to the Joint ICB Cluster Board on 14 September 2026 says the transition is “in all material respects, complete”: NHS England approved the phase one compulsory redundancy and phase two voluntary redundancy business cases on 21 August 2026, with formal notices and settlements issued from 1 September. The two Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) remain separate legal bodies with one shared leadership team.

events.headline: Birmingham and Solihull and Black Country Integrated Care Boards: legal merger anticipated in spring 2027, not yet confirmed
events.detail: Papers to the Joint ICB Cluster Board on 14 September 2026 describe the two Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) as separate statutory organisations “with legal merger anticipated in Spring 2027”. The July 2026 chief executive's report said NHS England was expected to decide final ICB footprints by September. As at 30/09/2026 NHS England has published no decision; its own page says future decisions on ICB footprints will be taken in light of Local Government Reorganisation.

events.headline: Birmingham and Solihull medicines committee now runs across the Black Country cluster: Hemant Patel sits as a cluster member
events.detail: At the Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Medicines Optimisation Committee (IMOC) on 9 July 2026, Integrated Care Board (ICB) members were listed for the first time as “Birmingham, Black Country and Solihull ICB (Cluster)”, including Hemant Patel, whom the Black Country ICB's own site names as Chief Pharmacy Officer and Director of Medicines and Clinical Policy. The minutes do not state his cluster-wide title, and the Birmingham and Solihull ICB's July 2026 board pack lists a “Chief Pharmacist MC & Deputy Chief Officer for Clinical Policy” post without naming its holder. The same meeting agreed that formulary chapter reviews should pause where needed so that medicines governance can be aligned across the cluster.

events.headline: Birmingham and Solihull formulary: Skin chapter reviewed, wider clinical changes to be made across the cluster
events.detail: The Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Medicines Optimisation Committee (IMOC) reviewed the formulary's Skin chapter on 9 July 2026. The review identified amendments including removal of brand names where more cost-effective generic or branded generic preparations are available. It agreed housekeeping amendments could proceed but that wider clinical and formulary changes should be made with stakeholders across the developing cluster. In February 2026 the committee agreed a reminder to primary care that emollients need clear dosing and administration instructions rather than “as directed”, particularly where carers apply them.
